resources.string: Use headphones: the microphone plays back through the speaker otherwise. The engine is the same C++ as the desktop console (libamix); audio I/O goes through AudioRecord / AudioTrack.
That QR code is not an AmF X1 pairing code. On the computer: NETWORK → PHONE REMOTE → START, then scan the code shown there.
The QR scanner is not available on this phone (it needs Google Play services). Use PAIR (PIN) instead.
On the computer: NETWORK → PHONE REMOTE → START. Type the six-digit PIN shown there (it changes every minute).
Type the console address first (shown on the computer under PHONE REMOTE).
Looking for consoles on this Wi-Fi…
No console found. On the computer: NETWORK → PHONE REMOTE → START (Wi-Fi), then FIND again.
Uses the saved console and pairing.
Forget the saved console and its pairing on this phone? To sign the phone out on the computer too, revoke it under NETWORK → PHONE REMOTE.
Keep the screen on while connected
Stopping the engine silences the whole console.
The app talks only to the console you pair with, on your own network. No accounts, no tracking, no cloud.
Put every setting back to its default? The saved console and pairing stay.
Stop the console\'s engine? All sound stops until a device is opened again.
Tap a channel name for trim, delay, EQ, dynamics and sends · tap MASTER for the limiter · long press a name to rename
Drag a dot: across for frequency, up and down for gain. Tap 1-8 or a dot to pick a band. Changes go to the console as you move; this phone remembers each strip\'s EQ.
Not connected: connect the remote first. You can still shape the curve; it is sent when you come back connected.
Console %1$s · saved %2$s (when the phone remote started)
The console has not saved its plug-in list yet: update the console, then start PHONE REMOTE again.
No plug-ins in any channel rack.
No VST plug-ins found. On the computer: PLUG-IN RACK → SCAN.
Read-only. While the phone remote runs, the remote service plays the audio, so racks and plug-ins are changed on the computer.
SAVE THE MIX AS A SCENE
No scenes on this phone yet. SAVE keeps the console\'s levels, pan, mute, solo, names, buses and master.
Recall \"%1$s\"? The console\'s faders, mutes, names and buses jump to it.
Recording stopped at %1$s. The file is in the console\'s recordings folder.
not offered by that computer: needs Windows 10 version 2004 or later
Eight groups kept on this phone. Tap a group to mute or un-mute all its channels; EDIT picks the channels.

Real-time analyzer: 31 third-octave bands from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, with peak hold. Levels are approximate dB SPL, using the SOUND LEVEL calibration; a phone microphone rolls off at the bottom and the top, so compare shapes rather than trusting absolute numbers.
Hi-res FLAC / WAV on the phone
The microphone or a USB interface, unprocessed, written by the AmF X1 engine.
The file could not be written. %1$s
This phone cannot play that file.
This input does not open at that rate: recording at 48 kHz.

Files are kept in the app\'s own folder (Android/data/com.amfb.amixos/files/recordings) and can be copied off over USB. 96 and 192 kHz need a microphone path or USB interface that offers them; the built-in microphone of most phones captures up to 48 kHz. Playback uses Android\'s own player.
Play one note near the phone. Green within 5 cents. Uses this phone\'s microphone; nothing is recorded or sent.
An estimate, not a calibrated meter: phone microphones differ by several dB. Set the calibration next to a real meter once (pink noise from GENERATOR works well).
Through the phone\'s output (plug it into a channel, or Bluetooth to a speaker). Start low: noise and sweeps at high level can damage tweeters and ears.
Allow the microphone to use this tool.
The microphone could not be opened.
Open MIXER, press FIND CONSOLE, then PAIR with the PIN the computer shows (NETWORK → PHONE REMOTE).
Pick several audio files (MP3, M4A, WAV, FLAC, OGG …). They play together, each at its own volume, and are exported as one AAC file. Nothing leaves the phone.
No files yet: press ADD FILES.
Mixed: %1$d KB, %2$.1f s. Choose where to save it.
Not saved (no place chosen). Press EXPORT again to save it.
Pick what the phone mixer opens. It runs through AAudio, Android\'s low-latency audio (what ASIO is on Windows).
whatever Android picks (follows headphones and Bluetooth)
A USB audio interface (class-compliant) appears here when plugged in through a USB-C or OTG adapter. If a chosen device is gone, the mixer falls back to the system route.
Every network interface of this phone with its real addresses.
Asks every local network this phone is on for an AmF X1 console (only its public status is read).
No console answered. Is it on the same network, with the phone remote switched on (NETWORK → PHONE REMOTE)?
%1$d console(s) found: tap one to use it for the remote.
What this phone\'s audio hardware layer offers, read through Android\'s public APIs and a short AAudio probe (nothing is played).
Tuning for this maker: the buffer the mixer asks for, and what stops audio in the background.
Keep audio running in the background
